sentences.text: 1 Advocate for Petitioner- Sri.Mohd Shesheriff Advocate for Respondent No.1-Sri.S.Maheswara advocate for Respondent No.2-Sri.Veerendra Patil  JUDGMENT
This claim petition is filed by the petitioners under Sec.166 of M.V Act, 1988 seeking compensation of Rs.75 lakhs for the death of Sanjay James caused in a road traffic accident.

2. The facts leading to the filing of top noted petition are that on 30-12-2018 at about 3.00 p.m.
when the Sanjay James was traveling in the car bearing No.KA-03-MQ-5676 near spice board mori No.229, near Donigala village, Sakaleshpura Taluk, Hassan district, at that time, driver of Bharat Benz tipper lorry bearing No.KA-35-B-4057 came with high speed and in a rash and negligent manner and dashed against the car, as a result of which Sanjay James sustained SCCH-6 MVC.
No.5849 of 2019 grievous injuries and succumbed to the injuries on the spot.

It is further stated that Sanjay James was working as SME (Subject Matter Expert) at Rentomojo, Bangalore and earning Rs.41,498/-p.m. and due to his death, petitioners lost the love and affection, lost the income and future income.
Hence prays to award compensation of Rs.75,00,000/- from the respondents.
3. Inspite of due service of notice to the respondents, both respondents appeared through their respective counsel and filed their respective written statement.
4. The respondent No.1 in its written statement contended that 2nd respondent has violated the section 134(c) and 158(c) of MV Act.
The deceased himself was solely negligent in causing the alleged accident.

The driver of the tipper lorry was not holding valid and effective DL as on the date of accident and further was not qualified for holding or obtaining such DL and not satisfied the requirements of the Rule 3 of the central MV rules 1989.
The Tipper lorry was not having valid permit and FC as on the date of accident.
Hence, prays to dismiss the petition.
SCCH-6 MVC. No.5849 of 2019 5.
2nd respondent in his written statement stated that driver of the offending vehicle who has valid DL which is valid till 12-4-2020 and policy is in force from 16-6-2019 to 15-6- 2019.

Further stated that the vehicle in question is registered with jurisdiction RTO on 25-8-2019 and FC is valid upto 24-8-2019 and having valid permit on the date of accident which is valid from 18-9-2018 to 17-9-2023.
It is further contended that the compensation claimed by the petitioners is exorbitant and without any basis, there is no negligence on the part of the respondent.
Hence respondent No.2 prays to dismissal of the claim petition.

6. On the basis of the above pleadings the following issues were framed :
ISSUES 1.
Whether the petitioners prove that they are the legal representative of the deceased?

sentences.text:
Whether the petitioners proves that Sanjay James S/o James K.B. died due to injuries sustained by him in an accident occurred on 30-12-2018 at about 9 p.m. near spice board mori No.229, near Donigala village, Sakaleshpur Taluk, Hassan district,
arising due to rash and negligent driving of driver of Tipper lorry bearing reg.No.KA-35-B-4057?
3. Whether the petitioners are entitled for compensation ? If so, how much and from whom ?
SCCH-6 MVC. No.5849 of 2019 4. What order or award ?

7. The Petitioner No.1 examined himself as PW.1 and.
Ex's.
P1 to 17
were marked on behalf of the petitioners.
one witness Nagesh Y.V. got examined as PW-2 and got marked Ex-P18 and 19.
One Nagesha V. got examined as PW-3 and got marked Ex-P20 to 28.

The respondent No.2 got examined himself as RW-1 and got marked Ex-R1 to Ex-R7.
8.
Arguments were addressed on both side.
9. Perused the entire materials placed on record.

My answers to the above issues are as follows :-
 Issue No.1 : In the Affirmative  Issue No.2 : In the Affirmative  Issue No.3 : Partly in the Affirmative  Issue No.4 : As per final order  for the following :
 REASONS 10. ISSUE NO.1 : In order to prove that the accident had occurred due to the actionable negligence on the part of the driver of the Tipper lorry bearing reg.No.KA-35- B-4057, the petitioner No.1 examined himself as PW.1 and  SCCH-6 MVC.

No.5849 of 2019 got marked 17 documents as Ex-P1 to 17 i.e.,FIR, complaint, inquest report, seizure mahazar, crime details form, IMV report, charge sheet, relieving letter, appointment letter, col.65 B letter, pay slip,
bank statement, bachelor of engineering certificate, pan card, adhaar card, identity card and income James K.B vs Cholamandalam Ms Gen Ins Co Ltd on 8 November, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/8265264/
3 tax returns.
11.

The evidence on record reveals that after the receipt of complaint lodged by petitioner No.1/James K.B. S/o Baby George Louis has lodged the complaint before the Sakaleshpura town police and detailed investigation and filed charge sheet as per Ex-P6 against the driver of the lorry bearing No.KA-35-B-4057 punishable u/s 279, 338, 304A of IPC by holding that on 30-12-2018 at about 3 p.m. when Rahul along with his friend Sanjay James and Aneesha D.Dsoza were coming from Donigal village in Maruthi baleno car bearing No.KA-03-MQ-5676 at that time one Tipper lorry bearing No.KA-35-B-4057 came from Sakaleshpura driven by its driver in high speed and negligent manner and hit to the Baleno car which was coming on the left side of the national highway near bridge No.229 and the SCCH-6 MVC.

No.5849 of 2019 lorry after hitting the car pushed the car, as a result of which the car fell into the ditch and the lorry fell on the top of the car,
as a result of which the car was completely damaged and the driver Rahul Joel and his friend Sanjay sustained severe injuries and succumbed.
Further the Anish Dsoza sustained grievous injuries.

Further it clearly shows that the driver of the lorry while turning in the curve road came to the extreme right side of the road and hit to the car which was coming on the left side and by pushing the car made the car to fell in the ditch.
Thereafter lorry also fell on the car.
Thus it clearly shows that the accident has been taken place due to the rash and negligent driving of the driver of the lorry.

12. Though respondent No.1 disputed the rash and negligent driving of the lorry and cause and manner of the accident but respondent has not examined the driver of the lorry who is the material witness to state about the facts and circumstances under which the accident has been taken place.
On the other hand, respondent No.2 owner of the offending vehicle examined himself as RW-1 and contended that on that day the lorry was driven by one Durgappa and SCCH-6 MVC.

No.5849 of 2019 was having valid licence and the driver of the vehicle drove the vehicle carefully by following all the traffic rules and accident has been caused only due to the sole rash and negligence of the deceased.
Further contended that the vehicle was having the valid insurance and permit and FC as on the date of the accident.
The driver of the vehicle in question is died on 19-5-2021 and produced the DL, RC, FC and permit and other documents.
In the cross examination admitted that the police have filed the charge sheet against the driver of the lorry.
The accident has been taken place due to the rash and negligence of the driver of the lorry.
There is nothing on record to believe that charge sheet is collusive and incorrect.
Moreover the respondent or the driver of the lorry has not at all challenged the charge sheet.
13. Apart from this, on perusal of IMV report marked at Ex- P5, it reveals that on that day the accident has not caused due to the any mechanical defect of the above said vehicles.

All these documents clearly shows that due to the sole rash and negligent driving of the driver of the lorry and in the said accident Sanjay James sustained grievous injuries and died SCCH-6 MVC. No.5849 of 2019 at the spot.
Under such circumstances, the evidence of PW.1 which is supported by police documents has to be accepted.

Consequently I hold that the accident is proved to have been caused due to the negligence of driver of the lorry bearing reg.No.KA-35-B-4057 and in the said accident Sanjay James sustained grievous injuries and died on the spot of accident.
As such, I answer issue No.1 in the Affirmative.

sentences.text: ISSUES NO.2 :
The petitioner No.1 filed affidavit in lieu of his chief-examination and deposed that he is the father, petitioner No.2 is his wife.

The petitioner has produced Ex-P13-pan card,
Ex-P14 to 16-Adhar cards.
The said documents reveals is the aforesaid relationship of the claimants with the deceased.
It is pertinent to note that this relationship of the petitioners with the deceased has not been disputed by the respondents, as it is evident from the tenor of cross-examination of PW.1.

Be that as it may, since the evidence led by PW.1 is satisfactory and also taking into consideration the fact that there are no rival claimants, I hold that the petitioners are the legal representatives of the deceased.
SCCH-6 MVC. No.5849 of 2019  15. LOSS OF DEPENDENCY INCLUDING FUTURE PROSPECTS:
In the Ex-P13-pan card the date of birth of deceased Sanjay James is shown as 23-12-1991, which indicates that he was aged 27 years as on the date of accident.

Therefore the appropriate multiplier as per Sarla Verma's case for the said age group of 26-30 is '17'.
16.
The petitioner contended that deceased was working as a SME (Subject Matter Expert) at Rentomojo, Bangalore and earning Rs.41,498/-p.m.

In support of his contention, petitioner examined Nagesha Y.V. is working as Deputy Manager, HDFC bank, Bangalore as PW-2 and produced the statement of account of the deceased from 1-4-2016 to 31-3-2019 as per Ex-P19.
17.

Further petitioner examined Nagesh V - Manager at Edunetwork (Rentomojjo) Private Limited as PW-3 who deposed that the deceased was working as a SME (Subject Matter Expert) and earning Rs.41,498/-p.m.

Further deposed that deceased joined services on 13-12-2016 and was working till the date of his death and produced the SCCH-6 MVC. No.5849 of 2019 appointment letter as per Ex-P21 to show that deceased was promoted to subject matter expert on 1-4-2018 and his salary was revised.

Further produced salary slips for the month of October, November and December 2018 as per Ex-P24, 23, 22 and also produced appointment letter as per Ex-P25 and form No.16 -Ex-P28 and the annexure 1 as Ex-P27.

On perusal of all these documents, it reveals that deceased was working in the Edunetwork (Rentomojjo) Private Limited since December 2016 till the date of his death and he was earning salary of Rs.33,356/-.
In November 2018 Rs.67,532/- and Rs.1,41,708/- in December 2018.
Thus there is a variation in the salary during October, November and December.
PW-3 was cross-examined at length by the counsel for the respondent No.1.
But nothing worth was elicited from his mouth to disprove his evidence.
It is pertinent to note here that no where the counsel for the respondent No.1 has denied that deceased was working at SME (Subject Matter Expert) at least by putting single suggestion.

Even it is material to note here that respondent has not at all denied the salary slips marked at Ex-P10 and SCCH-6 MVC. No.5849 of 2019 form No.16,
Ex-P27 and 28 documents.
Thus from the said documents, it is clearly shows that deceased was working at SME (Subject Matter Expert).
PW-3 has produced the form No.16 and annexure I attached to it which is marked as Ex- P27 and TDS copy marked as Ex-P28.

sentences.text: On perusal of which the annual income of deceased during the financial year 2018-2019 is Rs.2,93,829/-.
Hence this Court inclines to rely on the Ex-P27 and 28 for considering the annual income of the deceased.

Hence, from the above said documents, the annual income of the deceased for the financial year 2018-2019 is Rs.2,93,829/- and Rs.2,400/- is deducted towards the professional tax and the annual income is Rs.2,91,429/-.

The monthly income is Rs.2,91,429/-
divided by 12 is Rs.24,285=75 which is rounded off to Rs.24,286/-.
Hence income of the deceased is taken as Rs.24,286/-p.m.
As per Sarala Verma's case towards his future prospectus if 50% of the salary is added it would be around Rs.36,429/- (24286 + 12143).

Admittedly, the deceased was bachelor and as such in view of the proposition of Law laid down by the Hon'ble Supreme Court SCCH-6 MVC. No.5849 of 2019 in Sarla Verma's case, half of his income needs to be deducted towards personal & living expenses.
1/2 of Rs.36429/- works out to Rs.18215/-.
Income for consideration is Rs.18,214/- (36429- 18215).
Annual income works out to Rs.2,18,568/- (18214 X 12).
Appropriate multiplier is '17'.
Thus loss of dependency works out to Rs.37,15,656/- (2,18,568 X 17).
19. LOSS OF CONSORTIUM:

In view of the ratio laid by the Hon'ble Apex Court in (2021) 11 SCC 780 between United India Insurance Company Limited V/s. Satinder Kaur alias Satwinder Kaur and others, each of the claimants are entitled to a sum of Rs.48,400/- (in view of the Pranay Sethi case,
10% of Rs.40,000/- has to be enhanced for every 3 years from 2017) on account of loss of spousal consortium, parental consortium and loss of love & affection.

20. LOSS OF ESTATE: Petitioners are entitled for Rs.18,150/- ( in view of the Pranay Sethi case,
10% of Rs.15,000/- has to be enhanced for every 3 years from 2017) towards loss of estate.
SCCH-6 MVC. No.5849 of 2019 21.
FUNERAL EXPENSES:

Petitioners are entitled for Rs.18,150/- ( in view of the Pranay Sethi case,
10% of Rs.15,000/- has to be enhanced for every 3 years from 2017) towards funeral expenses.

22. The calculation table stands as follows :
1 Loss of Dependency : 37,15,656-00 2 Loss of Consortium : 96,800-00 3 Loss of Estate : 18,150-00 4 Funeral Expenses : 18,150-00 Total Rs.38,48,756=00 Hence,
petitioners are entitle for compensation of Rs.38,48,756=00.
23.
REGARDING INTEREST & LIABILITY:
Having regard to the nature of the claim and current bank rate of interest, this Tribunal is of the view that if interest at the rate of 6% p.a, is awarded it would meet the ends of justice.

24. Therefore, the respondent No.2 being the RC owner and respondent No.1 is the insurance policy holder of offending vehicle are jointly and severally liable to pay the aforesaid award amount to the petitioners together with SCCH-6 MVC. No.5849 of 2019 interest @ 6% p.a. from the date of claim petition till realization of the entire amount.

However the respondent No.1 being the insurer is primarily liable to satisfy the award amount together with interest within one month from the date James K.B vs Cholamandalam Ms Gen Ins Co Ltd on 8 November, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/8265264/

-: ORDER :-
The petition filed under Section 166 of Motor Vehicle's Act 1988, is hereby partly allowed with costs.
The petitioners are entitled for compensation of Rs.38,48,756=00 with interest at the rate of 6% p.a. from the date of petition till its realization.
The respondent No.1 is liable to pay and directed to deposit the compensation amount within a period of one month from the date of award.

 Petitioner No.1 30 - %

Out of the share amount of Petitioner No.1 and 2 a sum equal to 40% shall be deposited in their respective names in any Nationalized or Scheduled Bank of their choice for a period of 5 years and the remaining 60% shall be released to them through E-payment on proper identification and verification.
However the said petitioner No.1 and 2 are at liberty to withdraw the periodical interest accrued on their deposit amount from time to time.
Advocate fee is fixed at Rs.1,000/-.
Draw an award accordingly.
